reason: Mostly correct, and it is info only. Submits were at 05:28:13Z / 05:28:22Z, and poll.log headers come every ~602 s (11:11:11Z, then 11:21:13Z, ... 12:11:23Z, 12:21:25Z, ... 13:11:35Z, 14:21:49Z, 14:31:51Z). At the lowest insertion-family latency seen, 6.87 h (exp70a lower bound), completion is 12:20:3xZ and the first terminal header is 12:21:25Z, so the lower end holds. The upper end is slightly wrong: at 7.58 h (exp70b) completion is 13:03:10Z, so the first header showing it is ~13:11:35Z, not ~13:05Z. The 9.0 h clocks (14:28:13Z / 14:28:22Z), the 14:31Z fallback header and the 14:40Z ListSubmissions fallback match R15-A1 (4) and R16-A1 (3). Caveats: 6.87-7.58 h is an empirical span over n = 5 insertion-family runs, not a bound; exp57b (ungated insertion) has L in (6.72, 7.73]. A terminal at the 12:11Z header (L <= 6.72 h) is unlikely but not excluded, and ERROR can come at any moment. So '~12:10Z' should stay the conservative earliest edge, and the '~12:21Z' figure must not be used to delay the pre-score line. The finding's own action (land the line in or before the 12:00Z commit) is safe. The scan_plancheck PC17-02 wording 'practically by ~12:15Z' is not: it would miss the 12:11Z header. Round 16 already wrote '~12:10-13:10Z expected', so the news is small. There is no mechanism, submit or rule change, so R1-R10 and R8 are untouched and nothing closed is reopened. The finding has no score value; its only value is scheduling.

realistic_gain: No score gain (no private or public LB effect). Procedural only: it keeps the class-C letter window and the pre-score addendum correctly timed, and it prevents a later deadline being read into the ~12:21Z estimate. Risk if ignored: a small chance (~5%, if L <= 6.72 h or on an early ERROR) that the PC17-02/03 line lands after the first terminal header and counts as post-hoc.
